issues_found: A 2026 global-classical theorem allows zero logistic growth in 3D, so a logistic-only dismissal would be incorrect.
A 2026 Robin-boundary paper constructs actual blow-up; its full model and diffusion range needed checking.
Conditional blow-up rates can be mistaken for an example; eventual smoothness can be mistaken for smoothness throughout the earlier interval.
The general-domain formulation, time-zero data class and distinction from reaction–diffusion entry 315 needed preserving.
issues_resolved: PSX26 retains independent velocity dynamics and a different boundary condition even at zero logistic growth.
KA26 has an elliptic signal with Robin input; its counterexample also requires repulsion and sublinear diffusion.
Read the complete relevant JWZ18 and LW25 statements; neither establishes a matching counterexample or unconditional classical continuation.
Retained LW23 data/solution classes and LW25 general-domain scope; no extra uniform-in-time bound was imposed. Reread the nearest active entries and retained one higher-dimensional family.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Spatial mass-action reaction system with diagonal constant diffusion and reversible reaction terms. The candidate's directed flux −div(u grad v) is cross-diffusion and is not an included reaction term; the chemical is consumed without a reversible species network.
Existence of a chosen localized control for a scalar heat equation with cubic growth and Dirichlet conditions. Here no actuator is present and continuation of a coupled no-flux taxis system is asked.
Pathwise uniqueness for a one-dimensional stochastic mild equation. The candidate is deterministic, n≥3, and asks global classical existence.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: A separate nutrient-driven migration model and unconditional classical-continuation question. Count one canonical family across all n≥3, domain geometries and initial sizes.
implications_or_equivalences: Classical continuation excludes finite-time loss of the specified solution class; no claim that every known weak solution is unique or immediately regular.
The signal-production Keller–Segel system has a different second equation and its blow-up results do not transfer.

applied_significance: Cells or bacteria diffuse and move toward higher nutrient concentration while consuming that same nutrient. The question tests whether this closed-domain continuum model always supplies finite classical concentration fields over each observation interval despite the concentrating taxis flux. Consumption bounds the signal itself, but does not directly control its gradient or cell aggregation.

proposed_statement:
Let $n\ge3$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth boundary. Let $u_0,v_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$, with $u_0\ge0$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, and $v_0>0$ on $\overline\Omega$. Consider

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_tu&=\Delta u-\nabla\!\cdot(u\nabla v),\\
\partial_tv&=\Delta v-uv
\end{aligned}
\qquad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,\infty),
$$

with homogeneous Neumann conditions $\partial_\nu u=\partial_\nu v=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal, and initial values $(u,v)|_{t=0}=(u_0,v_0)$.

Does the maximal local classical solution extend to all positive times for every such domain and initial pair, without any smallness assumption? The required solution class is

$$
\begin{aligned}
u&\in C^0(\overline\Omega\times[0,\infty))
       \cap C^{2,1}(\overline\Omega\times(0,\infty)),\\
v&\in C^{2,1}(\overline\Omega\times(0,\infty))
       \cap\bigcap_{n<q<\infty}C^0([0,\infty);W^{1,q}(\Omega)),
\end{aligned}
$$

with $u\ge0$ and $v>0$ for positive times. Here $C^{2,1}$ means continuous spatial derivatives through order two and a continuous first time derivative; the equations and boundary conditions hold pointwise. The initial conditions are attained in the displayed spaces. No derivative compatibility at time zero is imposed beyond these data assumptions. [1]

Both diffusivities, the attraction coefficient and the consumption coefficient are fixed at one. The question concerns classical continuation through every finite time; a uniform bound as $t\to\infty$ or a specified convergence rate is not an additional requirement. All dimensions $n\ge3$ form one problem family. [1, 3, 6]
